items.text:
In preparation for the arrival of TYPHOON CHAMPI, the U.S. Coast Guard Captain of the Port (COTP) Forces Micronesia/Sector Guam has established PHWC ZULU for the Ports of Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan, Tinian, and Rota) effective 0700 CHsT, 17 October 2026.
In accordance with Title 33, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Part 160.111(c), the COTP hereby orders the following:
All commercial vessels are directed to suspend operations. Owners/operators must ensure that
their vessels are secured at a safe facility/location.
All maritime related transfers of cargo, oil, or hazardous materials are suspended within the Ports
of Saipan & Tinian.
All marinas are closed to recreational traffic.
All commercial vessels with written approval from the COTP to remain in port must ensure that moorings are secure and checked/adjusted as necessary. Report any unusual conditions or damage to the Harbormaster as soon as possible using VHF 16.
The COTP has closed the Ports of Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan, Tinian, and Rota), to include the territorial seas as defined by Title 33, CFR, Part 2.22(a), 12
miles around Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan, Tinian, and Rota), prohibiting any vessel movement or waterside port facility operations without specific written approval of
the COTP. This closure will remain in effect until lifted by the COTP. Any questions or concerns regarding this matter should be forwarded to the USCG Forces Micronesia/Sector Guam Command Center at (671) 355-4824. For general questions concerning the storm's predicted track, speed, or intensity, please contact the National Weather Service at 211 or (671) 472-0900.

items.text:
To All Shipping Agents, Vessels Masters, Facility Operator, and Partner:
1. In preparation for the arrival of TROPCIAL DEPRESSION 29W, the U.S. Coast Guard Captain of the Port
(COTP) Forces Micronesia/Sector Guam has established PHWC X-RAY for the Ports of Guam and the
Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan, Tinian, and Rota) effective 1600 CHsT, 15
October 2026. Vessel transits within the Port of Tinian remain restricted to daylight hours only.
In accordance with Title 33, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Part 160.111 (c), the COTP hereby
orders the following:
2. Shoreside facilities, terminals, and commercial vessels greater than or equal to 200 gross tons
must begin preparations to complete cargo operations and non-approved vessels shall prepare to
depart the Ports of Guam and CNMI. "Dead" ships or vessels/barges unable to put to sea must
make a prompt written application to the COTP (see enclosure (l ).
3. Upon the establishment of PHWC Yankee, all commercial vessels greater than or equal to 200
gross tons must depart and inbound vessels are prohibited from entering port without specific
written approval. Based upon current projections, please anticipate potential for PH WC Yankee
to be set on Friday, October 16, 2026.
4. Upon establishment of PHWC Zulu, the port and marinas will be closed to maritime traffic, and
all cargo and bunker operations will be suspended. No maritime-related terminal, facility, vessel,
or marina operations will be permitted until further notice. All vessels are reminded to resubmit
or update their electronic notice of arrival prior to re-entering when the port reopens.
5. Any vessel or facility operator desiring a COTP waiver from the above restrictions must submit a written
request using enclosure (l) via email to preventionguam@uscg.mil. If you have questions or concerns,
please call the Sector Guam Command Center at (671) 355-4824. For general questions concerning the
storm's predicted track, speed, or intensity, please contact the National Weather Service at 211 or (671) 472-0900.
